text: This is OpenRampKit, open-source deposit infrastructure for crypto apps. Getting users onchain is easy now. Getting them funded is the hard part, and that's where most of them drop off. This playground runs the real server right here in your browser, with mock providers.
Let's start with a user in Singapore. Under Use Cash, they see the methods people actually use there. They pick PayNow and enter two hundred dollars.
The planner asks every provider for a quote, and shows the fees up front. The best price comes first.
Now they scan the QR code with their banking app. Since this is test mode, we simulate the payment.
And that's it, the deposit is complete. Your page gets widget events, and your backend gets a signed webhook.
Next, a user in the United States. Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay are right there. They pick card, and compare quotes.
They type in the test card, right inside the widget, and pay.
Some people keep their funds on an exchange. So there's also a deposit address, with the network and the token, and they send USDC from their exchange account.
You decide which payment sources to offer. Turn off card, and it's gone. Then make it match your brand, with a theme, corners and a font.
The same kit handles the way out. Here a user withdraws USDC to GCash, in the Philippines, and gets a payout quote in local currency.
They enter their details, approve one transaction in their wallet, and the provider pays out.
Your ops team gets an admin dashboard too. Every deposit and withdrawal, stuck payments, webhook replays, and a note on every manual fix.
For developers, it's just a few lines. Create a session on your server, and open the widget on your page.
There are thirteen provider adapters, from card onramps to local rails. It's self-hosted, right next to your own backend.

Settlement is onchain. The same contract is live on Tempo, Arbitrum and Robinhood Chain testnets, and one transaction emits a Settled event your app can verify. It works with Solana and any EVM chain.
AI agents can use it too. Through MCP, an agent creates a pay link, and a person pays. OpenRampKit is open source and MIT licensed. Let's get your users onchain.
